brief: Mizuho sees oil-driven pressure defining the week: Brent above $106 after Gulf-Iran talks are postponed and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is shut following a drone attack, with Houthi control of Bab al-Mandeb raising double-chokepoint risk, keeping energy prices and the bearish duration impulse alive. Stronger CPI has markets pricing an 86% chance of a Fed hike Wednesday and 90bp of 2026 tightening; Mizuho expects at least two hikes, risks skewed to more and front-loaded, and says a hawkish Fed plus further oil upside could push 10Y UST toward 5%, so it stays cautious on duration into the meeting. In EUR rates, Lagarde's hawkish inflation warning does not resolve the tension between energy inflation and demand destruction above $100 oil; Mizuho is more dovish than the market on the ECB and wary of chasing Bund yields (10Y above 3.50%) higher, while France's roughly EUR30bn savings plan argues against fading OAT underperformance. For Gilts, Mizuho expects a 6-3 BoE hold Thursday against market pricing of a November hike, and sees risk of a smaller QT envelope than the GBP50bn consensus, supportive at the long end, though near-term risk still favors higher front-end rates before an eventual receiving opportunity as UK growth weakens.
